name: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
history: The Church teaches that the Immaculate Mother of God, the ever-virgin Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory. Pope Pius XII defined this as a dogma of faith on 1 November 1950. It is one of the oldest feasts of Our Lady and a holy day of obligation.
life: Scripture does not describe the end of Mary’s life, but the Church in both East and West has long believed that she who bore Christ was not left to the corruption of the grave. In the East the feast of the Dormition, the falling asleep of the Mother of God, was kept by the sixth century, and the Emperor Maurice fixed it on 15 August. Rome adopted it in the seventh century. Pius XII, after consulting the bishops of the whole world, defined the dogma in the apostolic constitution Munificentissimus Deus. The definition does not settle whether Mary died before she was assumed, though the long tradition of East and West speaks of her falling asleep. The feast proclaims what God has done for Mary and promises what He will do for all the faithful: the resurrection of the body and life with God in body and soul.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, taken up into heaven, you are the sign of hope for the pilgrim Church. Look on us who still struggle on earth. Keep our eyes on the glory to which God calls us, help us to honour our bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit, and bring us home to your Son. Amen.
penance: Go to Mass today, a holy day of obligation, and pray the Glorious Mysteries of the Rosary, perhaps with your family.
meditation: Where Mary has gone, the Church hopes to follow. How would you live today if you truly believed your body, too, is made for glory?
prayer: Almighty, everlasting God, Who took up, body and soul, the Immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of Your Son, into heavenly glory, grant, we beseech You, that, always devoting ourselves to heavenly things, we may be found worthy to share in her glory. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
